result.title: Reserving Time and Taking Care at the Food Bank
result.objective: Learners will understand set aside and look after in context and use them naturally in new everyday situations.

exercises.prompt: In s1, 'The coordinator will set aside a short briefing before the food-bank opens on Saturday,' what does 'set aside' mean?

options.text: to reserve time for a briefing
options.explanation: Correct: it matches reserving time for a specific purpose in s1.

options.text: to cancel a briefing because there is no time
options.explanation: Wrong: s1 is about arranging time, not cancelling the briefing.

options.text: to move a briefing to a later date
options.explanation: Wrong: s1 is about reserving time, not postponing it to later.

exercises.explanation: Only a matches the source meaning of reserving time for a purpose.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural sentence using 'set aside' to talk about reserving time or money.

options.text: They set aside some money each month for pay their bills.
options.explanation: Wrong: for pay should be for paying to use a gerund after for.

options.text: They set aside some money each month for their holiday.
options.explanation: Correct: set aside with an object and for plus noun phrase is natural.

options.text: They set aside some money each month to saving for the future.
options.explanation: Wrong: to saving should be to save to use infinitive after to.

exercises.explanation: Only b uses correct grammar with set aside.

exercises.prompt: In s2, 'New volunteers will learn where to store donated goods and how to look after chilled items,' what does 'look after' mean?

options.text: to look at chilled items quickly without touching them
options.explanation: Wrong: s2 is about taking care of items, not just glancing at them.

options.text: to take care of chilled items and keep them in good condition
options.explanation: Correct: it matches taking care of something and keeping it in good condition.

options.text: to carry chilled items to a different shelf
options.explanation: Wrong: s2 is about caring for items, not moving them elsewhere.

exercises.explanation: Only b matches the source meaning of taking care of something.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural sentence using 'look after' to talk about taking care of something.

options.text: My neighbour look after our plants when we are away.
options.explanation: Wrong: look should be looks to agree with the singular subject.

options.text: My neighbour looks after our plants when we are away.
options.explanation: Correct: looks after with a singular subject and object is natural.

options.text: My neighbour looks after to our plants when we are away.
options.explanation: Wrong: after to should be after to remove the extra preposition to.

exercises.explanation: Only b uses correct grammar with look after.

exercises.prompt: You are a neighbour asking another neighbour for help while you travel. Write 2-3 sentences asking them to take care of your plants and explaining what to do.
exercises.sampleAnswer: I will be away next weekend. Could you please look after my plants and water them every morning?
selfCheck: I used look after in a correct form to talk about taking care of something.
My request is polite and clearly explains the task.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
